The user wants to know if the application automatically detects when the LSP server crashes or stops responding and restarts it without user intervention.

I have three completed jobs (T1, T2, T3).
T1 and T2 asked where the detection and restart happen. They found `restart lsp for workspace`, `schedule debounced lsp restart`, `completion wait timeout ms`, `on transport reader eof`, `set reader eof handler`, `start`.
T3 asked what event or error triggers the restart. It found that `transport reader eof` only cleans up state (`ready false waitpid`) and does *not* trigger a restart. It also found that `restart lsp for workspace` is invoked manually or by configuration, not by the transport EOF.

The "Cerrado" of T3 explicitly states: "no encontré el mecanismo de reinicio automático tras error de transporte; lo leído muestra que transport reader eof solo limpia estado ready false waitpid sin disparar reinicio, y que restart lsp for workspace es invocado manualmente o por configuración, no por el EOF del transporte".

This directly refutes the user's claim that the application *automatically* detects and restarts the LSP server when it crashes or stops responding (
